title: Card Security Alert
topic: A freeze notice that treats a flag as near-certainty
blurb: Dinner was declined. The bank's support AI drafted a freeze notice.
prompt: A bank support AI auto-drafted this freeze notice. If a line doesn't follow from the facts, tap it.

segments.label: How rare
segments.text: Only 1 in every 1,000 charges on this card network is actually fraudulent.

segments.label: The catch rate
segments.text: Our AI flags 99% of the charges that really are fraud.

segments.label: The false alarms
segments.text: On legitimate charges, it raises a false alert only 1% of the time.

segments.label: The jump
segments.text: So whenever the AI flags a charge, there is a 99% chance it is real fraud.

segments.label: The action
segments.text: Agents should freeze the account immediately, no need to ping the customer first.

conclusion: AI verdict: A flagged charge is 99% likely to be real fraud. Freeze first, ask later.

flaws.original: Out of 1,000 charges, roughly 1 real fraud and about 10 legitimate dinners get flagged, so an alert is real fraud only about 9% of the time.
flaws.corrupted: So whenever the AI flags a charge, there is a 99% chance it is real fraud.

diagnosis_choices.label: It confuses 'catches 99% of fraud' with '99% of alerts are fraud.' Real fraud is so rare that false alarms outnumber true hits.
The catch rate and the false-alarm rate must add up to 50%, not 100%.
1 in 1,000 is 1%, so there should be 10 fraudulent charges per 1,000, not 1.

fix_choices.label: Count it out: of 1,000 charges, about 1 true fraud alert vs about 10 false alarms, so a flag is real fraud only ~1 in 11 (~9%).
Subtract the 1% false-alarm rate from 99% to get a 98% chance of fraud.
Multiply 99% × 99% to get a 98.01% chance of fraud.

flaws.explanation: Legitimate charges outnumber fraud 999 to 1. Even a 1% false-alarm rate produces about 10 innocent flags per 1,000 charges — ten times the single real fraud that's caught. So roughly 9 out of 10 alerts are someone trying to pay for dinner.
flaws.why_tempting: Our brains hear '99% accurate' and jump to 'a flag is 99% sure,' skipping how rare fraud is in the first place.
flaws.catch_rule: For a rare event plus a 'highly accurate' test, convert the percentages into headcounts out of 1,000 before trusting the headline.
flaws.hint: Out of 1,000 charges, how many perfectly innocent ones trigger that 1% false alarm?

practice.problem: An AI cheating detector flags 99% of real cheaters and 1% of honest students. If only 1 in 1,000 papers is actually cheated, roughly what share of flagged papers are true cheats?
practice.answer: About 1 in 11 (~9%): 1 true flag and ~10 false flags per 1,000 papers.

clean_segments: Only 1 in every 1,000 charges on this card network is actually fraudulent.
Our AI flags 99% of the charges that really are fraud.
On legitimate charges, it raises a false alert 1% of the time.
Out of 1,000 charges, about 1 real fraud and about 10 legitimate dinners are flagged, so an alert is real fraud only about 9% of the time.
Because most alerts are false alarms, ping the customer before freezing the account.
clean_conclusion: Even a 99% accurate detector, on a 0.1%-prevalence event, is wrong about 9 times out of 10.

diagnosis: One fraudulent charge per 1,000 is a 1% base rate.
The 999 other charges count as fraud in the base rate.
The base rate should equal the AI detection rate.
A 99% detection rate means only 1% of actual fraud is flagged.
The denominator for detection should include all charges.
Detection should be stated as 99 fraudulent charges per 1,000 total charges.
fix: Say it catches 1% of actual fraud.
Say it flags 99% of all charges as true fraud.
Say it catches 99 fraudulent charges per 1,000 total charges.

diagnosis: A 1% false alert rate means 99% of legitimate charges are flagged.
The rate should be expressed per actual fraudulent charge.
The false alert rate should be added to the fraud base rate to describe legitimate charges.
fix: Use a 99% alert rate on legitimate charges.
Define false alerts as 1% of actual fraudulent charges.
Replace the 1% rate on legitimate charges with 1.1%.

diagnosis: An immediate freeze means the transaction has already been refunded.
The recommendation applies to every legitimate charge, even without alerts.
A freeze requires closing the account permanently.
fix: Say the charge has already been refunded.
Apply the instruction to unflagged charges too.
Replace the temporary freeze with permanent closure.
